\section[o skate]{o skate — skateboard; skateboarding}

\label{lesson:PT-C507-skate}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for board, then the Portuguese for to surf.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o skate}
\textbf{o skate} — \textquotedblleft{}skateboard; skateboarding\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O rapaz vai para a escola de skate.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The boy goes to school on his skateboard.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Andar de skate} — to skateboard.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{skate} was borrowed from English \emph{skate} (EtymDB), which came from Dutch \emph{schaats}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o skate}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o skate}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o skate}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for board, then the Portuguese for to surf, then say \emph{o skate} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o skate mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Skateboard; skateboarding\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[patinar]{patinar — to skate}

\label{lesson:PT-C507-patinar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to surf, then the Portuguese for skateboard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: patinar}
\textbf{patinar} — \textquotedblleft{}to skate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No inverno patinamos no gelo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In winter we skate on the ice.}
\end{quote}

Of a car: to skid. \emph{O carro patinou na estrada}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{patinar} is usually traced to French \emph{patiner} \textquotedblleft{}to skate\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{patte} \textquotedblleft{}a paw\textquotedblright{}, a word whose origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{patinar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{patinar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{patinar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to surf, then the Portuguese for skateboard, then say \emph{patinar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does patinar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To skate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[os patins]{os patins — skates}

\label{lesson:PT-C507-patins}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for skateboard, then the Portuguese for to skate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: os patins}
\textbf{os patins} — \textquotedblleft{}skates\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Recebi uns patins no meu aniversário.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I got some skates for my birthday.}
\end{quote}

Singular \emph{o patim}. \emph{Patins em linha} — inline skates.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{patim} is usually traced to French \emph{patin} \textquotedblleft{}a skate\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{patte} \textquotedblleft{}paw\textquotedblright{}; the origin of \emph{patte} is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a caminhada]{a caminhada — (long) walk, hike}

\label{lesson:PT-C507-caminhada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to skate, then the Portuguese for skates.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a caminhada}
\textbf{a caminhada} — \textquotedblleft{}(long) walk, hike\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fizemos uma caminhada de dez quilómetros.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We went on a ten-kilometre walk.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer uma caminhada} — to go for a walk or a hike.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{caminhada} is built on \emph{caminho} \textquotedblleft{}path\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Late Latin \emph{camminus} \textquotedblleft{}a road\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced to a Celtic word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to skate, then the Portuguese for skates, then say \emph{a caminhada} again

\section[o alpinismo]{o alpinismo — mountaineering}

\label{lesson:PT-C507-alpinismo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for skates, then the Portuguese for (long) walk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o alpinismo}
\textbf{o alpinismo} — \textquotedblleft{}mountaineering\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O alpinismo é perigoso sem experiência.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mountaineering is dangerous without experience.}
\end{quote}

A climber is \emph{um alpinista}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{alpinismo} is built on the name of the Alps, the mountains where the sport grew up, with \emph{-ismo}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for skates, then the Portuguese for (long) walk, then say \emph{o alpinismo} again
